To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution patterns and receptive field properties of nerve dominance aggregates change within hours after injury of the nerves to primate hand.

nerve dominance aggregates in the hand area of somatosensory area 3b of monkeys begin changing within minutes of combined median and ulna nerve transection, that the changes involve expansion of the radial nerve dominance patches and a small expansion of the forelimb dominance patch, that the changes are highly consistent between animals and are arranged in a stereotyped pattern, and that the changes are not related to changes in the radial skin territory.
the cortical representations of the median and ulnar nerves of adult monkeys undergo a consistent and extensive expansion following injury of these nerves to the hand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the plasticity of the somatosensory system.
the plasticity of somatosensory maps of the hand in adult primates.
how the somatosensory system adapts to nerve injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nerve dominance patches in the hand area of the adult primate somatosensory hand area begin to change within minutes after injury of median and ulnar nerves.
the cortical representation of the radial nerve hand territory is expanded by the removal of competing inputs from the median and ulnar nerves.
nerve injury in adult primates initiates rapid, widespread, and specific alterations in the distribution of nerve dominance aggregates across the hand cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the somatosensory cortical map undergoes rapid, consistent, and highly specific early-onset alterations following injury of peripheral nerves to the hand.
the hand representation in somatosensory areas 3b and 1 of the adult monkey undergoes a rapid and consistent reorganization in response to nerve injury.
nerve injuries trigger rapid central changes in cortical representations, and that these changes may be important to the development of chronic neuropathic pain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cortical changes following injury occur within minutes of the injury, and are highly consistent across different monkeys.
the adult brain is highly plastic.
the adult somatosensory hand cortex is highly plastic and that this plasticity is initiated within minutes after nerve transection.
